recipes.name: Sloppy Steaks inspired by I Think You Should Leave with Tim Robinson
ingredients: 1 tsp kosher salt + more as needed
As needed black garlic, thinly sliced
As needed black radish, thinly sliced
instructions: For the Original Sloppy Steak
Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Generously season the steak with salt and pepper. Let sit at room temperature for 30 minutes. - as needed Salt - as needed Pepper
Add the oil to a large cast iron skillet. Preheat the skillet over high heat. - Oil
Add the steak to the preheated skillet and sear on both sides for 5 minutes.
Transfer the steak to a rack placed on a rimmed baking sheet.
Finish the steak in the preheated oven. Cook until the internal temperature reads 115°F, the carryover cooking will bring the temperature up to rare. Let the steak rest for 10 minutes.
While the steak rests, place an oven-safe serving platter in the oven.
Remove the platter from the oven and place the steak on it. Pour the glass of water over the steak. - glass of water
Serve immediately.
For the Dashi
Combine the kombu and water in a sealable container. Transfer it to the refrigerator and let it soak overnight. - 3 ½ pieces kombu (about 1/3 oz) - 1 quart water cold
Transfer the soaked kombu and the water to a medium pot. Bring the water to a boil over low heat.
Once at a boil, turn off the heat, remove the kombu, and add the bonito flakes. Let the dashi sit for 10 minutes. - 1 cup (loosely packed) bonito flakes
Strain the dashi through a fine-mesh sieve lined with paper towels or a clean dishcloth.
Reserve until ready to use.
For the ‘Sloppy’ Broth
Combine all the ingredients in a small pot. - 8 oz dashi broth - 3 tbsp mirin - 3 tbsp soy sauce - 2 tsp granulated sugar
Bring the sauce to simmer and cook until all the sugar has dissolved.
Turn off the heat and cover until ready to serve.
For the Lotus (Renkon) Chip
Preheat the oven to 350°F with convection.
Peel the lotus root using a vegetable peeler. - 1 fresh lotus root
Using either a mandolin or a sharp knife, cut ⅛ inch slices of the lotus root.

Combine the water, rice vinegar, and salt in a bowl or container. Transfer the lotus slices to the water to prevent discoloration. Let the slices sit for 10-15 minutes. - 1 quart water - 1 tbsp rice vinegar - 1 tsp kosher salt + more as needed
Strain and try the lotus slices on a sheet tray lined with paper towels.
Add a few tablespoons of oil to a large rimmed baking sheet. Coat the lotus slices in the oil and place them in the center of the sheet tray. - As needed vegetable oil
Coat the bottom of a small rimmed baking sheet with oil. Place the sheet tray over the lotus slices to weigh them down.
Bake the lotus slices for 5 minutes, then remove the small sheet tray. Make sure the slices are not stuck. Bake for another 4-5 minutes or until golden brown.
Remove the sheet tray from the oven and immediately transfer the lotus chips to a plate lined with paper towels.
Reserve the lotus chips until ready to use.
For the Wasabi Sauce
Combine the wasabi powder, mirin, and sugar in a small bowl. - ⅓ cup wasabi powder - 2 tsp mirin - ½ tsp granulated sugar
Alternate adding the water and oil, whisking well between each addition, until you’ve reached your desired thickness and consistency. - ½ cup water - ½ cup neutral oil
Reserve until ready to use.
For the Sloppy Shabu
Cut the steak into slices about 1 inch thick and 3-4 inches long. - 5 oz A5 wagyu ribeye steak
Heating binchotan charcoal using a charcoal chimney. Transfer the heated binchotan to a ceramic yakitori grill.
Once the grill is heated, add the steaks and cook for 1 minute on each side.
Let the steak rest for 5 minutes, then slice it into thin pieces for serving.

Plate the steak with the shiso leaf, enoki mushrooms, carrot, black garlic, black turnip, wasabi sauce, lotus chip, gold leaf, and maldon salt. - 1 shiso leaf - As needed carrot thinly sliced - As needed enoki mushrooms - As needed black garlic thinly sliced - As needed black radish thinly sliced - Reserved wasabi sauce - Reserved lotus chip - As needed gold leaf - As needed maldon salt
Finally, pour the sloppy broth over the steak and enjoy. - Reserved sloppy broth
